key_insight: RNADyn introduces a standardized benchmark for RNA dynamics, making it possible to evaluate models on both generating realistic RNA motions and understanding RNA conformational behavior. It addresses the gap between static RNA structure prediction and true dynamic modeling.
problem_solved: RNA biology depends on time-varying conformations, but high-quality, large-scale, standardized dynamics data are scarce. Existing methods often split trajectory generation and dynamics understanding into separate tasks, making fair evaluation difficult and risking data leakage across train/test splits.
method: Build RNADynBench, a benchmark containing 2,585 quality-controlled all-atom RNA molecular dynamics trajectories, each 100 ns long.
Use leakage-controlled dataset splits to support rigorous and fair evaluation of model generalization.
Unify generation and understanding of RNA dynamics under a single benchmark framework for standardized comparison.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, RNADyn provides a reliable testbed for developing and comparing models that learn molecular motion, not just static structure. It helps reduce overfitting and leakage, enabling more trustworthy progress in biomolecular generative modeling and representation learning.

paper_title: RNADyn: A Benchmark for Generating and Understanding RNA Dynamics
paper_authors: Yiming Huang, Lennart Bastian, Hanqun Cao, Luis Vollmers, Tolga Birdal
